prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Production pixel-art UI sprite atlas for a forest tower-defense game, with TRUE TRANSPARENT ALPHA background. Image 1 is the exact style reference for brown leather numbered banners, circular stone platform and faceted gold/dark stars. Image 2 is the style reference for silver crossed chains and a cream iron padlock. Image 3 shows intended in-game look; use its compact pixel detail. Create a square 1536x1536 atlas in a STRICT 3 columns by 3 rows grid of equal 512x512 cells. Each cell contains ONE isolated sprite centered with at least 48px transparent margins. No printed grid, checkerboard, labels, ground, scene or cast shadow. Row 1 cells: standalone hanging leather banner with numeral '1', identical banner with '2', identical banner with '3'. Row 2 cells: identical banner '4', identical banner '5', one circular mossy gray stone pedestal viewed slightly from above (wide ellipse, pale top masonry rim and dark stone sides). ALL FIVE BANNERS must be the SAME shape, size and position within their cells, with wooden horizontal bar, golden rod ends, rich orange-brown leather, pointed bottom, off-white bold pixel numerals dark-outlined. Banner cells have NO platform, lock, chains or stars. Row 3 cells: ONE golden five-point faceted star; ONE dark charcoal unearned five-point star, same silhouette and size; ONE standalone overlay composed of two silver chains crossing in an X behind a central cream iron padlock with black keyhole. The overlay contains ONLY lock and chains with transparent holes, NO banner, question mark, number or pedestal. Bold crisp dark pixel outlines, manually shaded blocky pixel clusters, match references closely. Never render the reference checkerboard as image pixels; transparency must be real. No text other than exactly the five numerals on banners.
